image_prompt.text: One massive stylized mountain about 1000x1000 studs at the base, built from blocky block-and-wedge parts into a stepped, terraced landform rising to a high central peak, banded into a grassy base, rocky mid-slopes and a snow-capped summit
Multiple winding roads switchbacking up the mountain from the base to the summit, each at least 20 studs wide so vehicles can drive them, with guardrails running along the outer edges of every turn
The snow-capped peak rising high in the centre, readable from anywhere on the slopes so a driver always knows which way is up
Flat plateaus and pull-offs spaced along the switchback roads, composed as viewpoints looking back down over the terraced slopes

notes: Stage A landed on None: this is a place, not a game type. There is no race, lap, finish line or opponent anywhere in it — 'suitable for driving' is the intended use and 'similar to a Roblox tycoon or driving game environment' is an aesthetic reference — so it was deliberately not routed to Racing. It was a close call and is recorded here in case a genre surfaces later.

Preset caveat: kept Explorable Place and all three of its options, but replaced its all-default shape. Verticality is 'tiered' because the mountain is explicitly terraced with a peak, and structure is 'must-be-valid' because the switchback roads have to genuinely connect base to summit at a drivable width — a road that dead-ends mid-slope fails the request outright, and that is not something an image model can guarantee.

No caves, tunnels, bridges or overhangs are described, so verticality stays 'tiered' rather than 'stacked' and the build stays off P2. Enclosure, zone count and play-space are all at their defaults: one continuous exterior surface, nothing entered, nothing flown or swum through.

Requested as editable attributes, which no layout option can carry: mountain height, road width, number of switchback turns, base (grass) colour, rock colour, snow colour, road colour. Passed through for whoever builds the parametric version.

would have asked: Sounds like an environment showcase — one big terraced mountain as the landmark, the switchback roads as the circulation through it, and the plateaus as viewpoints along the way. I'd build it with real stepped elevation and treat the road network as structure that has to be valid rather than just dressed, since it has to actually be drivable end to end. Want that, or would you rather assemble it yourself?

would have asked: The roads being genuinely connected and drivable from base to summit is the one thing I'm treating as load-bearing rather than decorative — confirming that is right. Also worth a yes/no: a gathering area at the summit, an open flat space at the top sized for a crowd of cars to park up in, is the one signature option you don't already have.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
